summary: Established a site-to-site IPsec (IKEv2, AES256/SHA256) tunnel between node1 (VyOS, transit 10.10.3.1) and node2 (OPNsense, transit 10.10.3.2), carrying lan-a (10.10.1.0/24, node3 behind node1) and lan-b (10.10.2.0/24, node4 behind node2) across it. node3 and node4 reach each other by their private addresses (10.10.1.10 <-> 10.10.2.10) with traffic encrypted in transit (verified only ESP frames cross the transit wire). All configuration is persisted (VyOS config saved to config.boot; OPNsense config.xml with Swanctl connection/PSK/firewall rules; NetworkManager static routes on node3/node4; an rc.syshook boot script on node2 for its static route to lan-a). All four nodes were restarted one at a time with confirmed changed boot identity and full post-restart recovery of the tunnel, routes, and end-to-end connectivity.
actions_performed: Discovered topology: node1 (VyOS) eth1=transit 10.10.3.1/24, eth2=lan-a 10.10.1.254/24; node2 (OPNsense) opt1/vtnet1=transit 10.10.3.2/24, opt2/vtnet2=lan-b 10.10.2.254/24; node3 enp8s0=10.10.1.10/24; node4 enp8s0=10.10.2.10/24. Verified L2 pairing via ARP/tcpdump.
Configured static addressing on node3/node4 via nmcli (persistent) and on node1 via VyOS set interfaces (saved).
Configured node2 opt1/opt2 interface assignment and addresses via config.xml + configctl interface reconfigure.
Generated a PSK on node2 via openssl rand, transferred it into node1's configuration via secret_env only (never in literal command text or this report), then deleted the temp file.

Configured VyOS IPsec: ike-group/esp-group (aes256/sha256/dh14, ikev2), a global PSK object keyed by transit IPs, and site-to-site peer NODE2 with tunnel 1 local/remote prefixes 10.10.1.0/24 <-> 10.10.2.0/24. Committed and saved.

Configured OPNsense IPsec via config.xml surgery under OPNsense/Swanctl (Connection/local/remote/child) and OPNsense/IPsec/preSharedKeys, plus legacy ipsec/enable flag. Reloaded via configctl ipsec reload.

Diagnosed and fixed three separate blockers: (1) OPNsense default-deny pf blocking IKE/ESP on the transit interface -> added explicit pass rules for udp/500, udp/4500, esp on opt1; (2) duplicate/racing IKE_SAs from 'unique: no' -> set unique=replace and cleared stale SAs; (3) missing route to the remote LAN on node2 causing 'no route' silently dropping return ICMP (FreeBSD requires a FIB route to trigger SPD) -> added static route; (4) OPNsense's default deny also blocks decrypted tunnel traffic re-entering on the virtual enc0 interface ('block in on enc0') and the modern Firewall/Filter interface field rejects enc0/IPsec as a valid interface -> added a legacy filter rule with a blank interface (applies to all interfaces) to permit the decrypted tunnel traffic.

Verified end-to-end: node3 <-> node4 ping succeeds in both directions; swanctl SA byte/packet counters increment correctly; tcpdump on the transit link (node1 eth1) shows only ESP frames traversing the wire.
Persisted routes for reboot survival: node3/node4 via nmcli ipv4.routes; node2 via an rc.syshook.d/start script re-adding the static route to lan-a at boot.

Ran the mandatory restart protocol: captured boot_id/kern.boottime and healthy IPsec/ping baselines on all 4 nodes, restarted node1, node2, node3, node4 one at a time (native reboot/shutdown -r), polled each until exec was available again, confirmed a new boot identity each time, and verified full recovery (IPsec re-established, firewall rules recompiled, routes present, cross-network ping working) before moving to the next node.

evidence.requirement: IPsec tunnel established between node1 and node2
evidence.summary: swanctl -l on both node2 and node1 shows IKE_SA ESTABLISHED (IKEv2, AES_CBC-256/HMAC_SHA2_256_128) and CHILD_SA INSTALLED with local/remote traffic selectors 10.10.1.0/24 <-> 10.10.2.0/24.

evidence.requirement: node3 and node4 reach each other via private addresses
evidence.summary: ping from node3 (10.10.1.10) to node4 (10.10.2.10) and reverse both succeed with 0% packet loss after routes and firewall rules were fixed.

evidence.requirement: Traffic is encrypted in transit across the transit network
evidence.summary: tcpdump on node1's transit interface (eth1) during a node3->node4 ping shows only ESP packets between 10.10.3.1 and 10.10.3.2 on the wire; the plaintext lines shown are the local post-decrypt view on the same netdevice, not separate wire traffic.

evidence.requirement: Root-cause fixes for tunnel not passing traffic
evidence.summary: Sequence showing diagnosis and fix of default-deny blocking IKE/ESP, duplicate SA unique=replace fix, missing FIB route causing ICMP no-route errors, and the enc0 'block in' firewall gap resolved by an all-interface pass rule for decrypted tunnel traffic.

evidence.requirement: Node1 (VyOS) restart baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 01e92881...; reboot acknowledged and returned before disconnect; new boot_id 81571a82... confirms restart; swanctl ESTABLISHED and node3->node4 ping succeed post-restart.

evidence.requirement: Node2 (OPNsense) restart baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline kern.boottime 05:18:07; reboot acknowledged; new kern.boottime 05:42:06 confirms restart; post-restart shows persisted static route, recompiled firewall rules, re-established IPsec SA, and successful node3->node4 ping.

evidence.requirement: Node3 (RHEL10) restart baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 434803ac...; reboot acknowledged; new boot_id 31cc1790... confirms restart; persisted route present and ping to node4 succeeds post-restart.

evidence.requirement: Node4 (RHEL10) restart baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 73237116...; reboot acknowledged; new boot_id 4fdd2f72... confirms restart; persisted route present and ping to node3 succeeds post-restart.

evidence.requirement: Final full-system verification after all four restarts
evidence.summary: Post-all-restarts check shows IPsec SA established with correct traffic selectors on node1, and successful bidirectional ping between node3 and node4.
